diagnostic_excluded_from_qualification.cause: The test omitted NeverC’s existing explicit -fllvm-backend selection for i386 objects. Its embedded machine backend is x64-only.

limits: One runtime-backed C dispatch route over already admitted instructions. This does not add an instruction bank or ordinary i386 function decompilation, HighC/LLVMC arithmetic projection, IA-32e compatibility, real/VM86 or task execution.
Selections require complete 1..15-byte nonwrapping image extents. Live CS-base linear wrap is supported; wrapping the selected image extent past 4 GiB is rejected.

The matching C++ embedding owns and retains state, RAM, runtime profiles, device/debug callbacks and event arbitration. There is no serialized public C state ABI, native snapshot capture or inferred asynchronous event producer.
Generated C was executed on Linux x64. ELF32/i386 objects were independently checked as relocatable little-endian EM_386 files; a 32-bit host runtime bridge was not executed.

The new branch oracle uses Linux ptrace on the recorded Intel P/E core classes and compares PC, accumulator/count, defined arithmetic/DF flags and stack delta. Software assertions separately inspect debug/event state. It does not qualify raw full-machine BTF, CPL0 hardware, task/RTM debug or physical port I/O.
The full paging suite explicitly skips one LA57 hardware case because the bound KVM CPU lacks LA57. Software coverage is not substituted for that hardware result.

Both build profiles disable the embedded Python plugin host. Raw Python C API calls are executed against both actual SDKs; NeverDPythonRuntimeTests and NeverDPythonPluginTests are unavailable in these profiles.

Global instruction/state/source coverage, software SMM/SGX and remaining fault, asynchronous-event and environment contracts are still incomplete. This qualification does not authorize a claim of global completion.
